n344ee6e2a25.s: In which year did the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State Relations submit its report?
n344ee6e2a25.x: The Commission on Centre-State Relations reported in 2010; it was appointed by the Government of India in 2007.

nbca9826e54f.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended a constitutional amendment giving the Governor how long to decide on Bills passed by the State Assembly?
nbca9826e54f.x: Punchhi proposed a constitutional amendment prescribing a six-month period for the Governor to decide on Bills.

n60b609bfe11.s: Which of the following Punchhi Commission recommendations on the Governor is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 156 – delete 'during the pleasure of the President'
Removal – impeachment by the State Legislature
Model for removal – impeachment of the President
Transfer – periodic rotation of Governors among States
n60b609bfe11.x: Punchhi wanted the pleasure clause removed and impeachment-style removal like the President's; periodic rotation of Governors was not its recommendation.

n2c75b74f3c0.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that the National Integration Council should meet at least:
n2c75b74f3c0.x: Punchhi wanted the National Integration Council to meet at least once a year; thrice a year was for the Inter-State Council.

n0172801c3b0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: It was first chaired by M. Veerappa Moily
V. Ramachandran later became its chairman
n0172801c3b0.x: The Second ARC was constituted in 2005; 1966 is the year of the First ARC.

na0345b3a265.s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up?
na0345b3a265.x: The Inter-State Council came in 1990, after the Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) and before the Punchhi Commission (2007-10).

n21dc83675ab.s: The CEO of NITI Aayog is:
o: A Union Cabinet Minister with no fixed tenure
A Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure
A part-time member chosen by rotation
n21dc83675ab.x: NITI Aayog's CEO is a Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure; the Prime Minister is its Chairperson.

nindian-polity-65-3.s: Which of the following is a statutory body, created by an Act of Parliament?
nindian-polity-65-3.x: Statutory bodies such as the NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are created by legislation; NITI Aayog and the Planning Commission came by Cabinet resolution and the Election Commission is constitutional.

n05f6965b374.s: The 2016 committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments was convened by:
n05f6965b374.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu convened the 2016 digital-payments committee, which was separate from the three 2015 NITI Aayog sub-groups.

n2a205eb5132.s: The GST Council is provided for in which Article of the Constitution?
n2a205eb5132.x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council, where the Centre holds one-third and the States two-thirds of the votes.

n3b6b0d14ded.s: Which of the following pairs of Chief Ministers' committee and convener is NOT correctly matched?
o: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2015) – N. Chandrababu Naidu
Rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes (2015) – Parkash Singh Badal
n3b6b0d14ded.x: The sub-group on rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes was convened by Shivraj Singh Chouhan; Badal convened Skill Development.

new.s: Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, Chairman of the Commission on Centre-State Relations, was a former:
o: Chief Justice of a High Court
new.x: Justice M.M. Punchhi was a former Chief Justice of India, not a retired High Court judge.

new.s: Which of the following was a member of the Punchhi Commission?
new.x: Dr N.R. Madhava Menon was a member along with Dhirendra Singh, Vinod Kumar Duggal and Vijay Shanker; Sarkaria and Rajamannar headed earlier bodies.

new.s: The Punchhi Commission was to review Centre-State arrangements in the light of changes since the:
new.x: Its mandate was to review arrangements in the light of changes since the Sarkaria Commission (1983-88), such as Panchayati Raj, reforms, coalition politics and internal security.

new.s: The Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations (1969) was set up by the:
new.x: Rajamannar is the only one of the three commissions set up by a State – Tamil Nadu; Sarkaria and Punchhi were set up by the Centre.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Punchhi Commission
2. Rajamannar Committee
3. Sarkaria Commission
new.x: Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983), Punchhi (2007).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about commissions on Centre-State relations:
1. The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 and reported in 1988.
2. The Rajamannar Committee was appointed by the Centre.
3. The Punchhi Commission recommended that the Inter-State Council meet at least thrice a year.
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Rajamannar Committee was appointed by the Tamil Nadu government.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a Punchhi Commission recommendation on the Governor?
o: A fixed tenure of five years
Removal by impeachment by the State Legislature
Governors should not be Chancellors of State universities
Abolition of the office of Governor
new.x: Punchhi did not recommend abolishing the office of Governor; the other three were its recommendations.

new.s: The Punchhi Commission wanted the Governor to be an eminent person who had not been in active politics, even at the local level, for:
o: A couple of years before appointment
Five years after the end of tenure
new.x: It recommended an eminent person not in active politics, even locally, for a couple of years before appointment.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Punchhi Commission's view on Articles 355 and 356?
o: Article 356 should be used only as a last resort
There is no need to amend Articles 355 and 356
Article 356 should never be used in a partisan way
A localised emergency may cover a district or part of a district
new.x: Punchhi recommended amending both Articles 355 and 356; 'no need to amend' is the APPSC 2017 trap.

new.s: Under the Punchhi recommendation on deploying central forces in communal violence, the State's consent is to be obtained:
o: Only after the State Assembly passes a resolution
new.x: The Centre may deploy central forces suo motu for a short period without prior consent, and the State's consent is obtained afterwards.

new.s: Deploying central armed forces in States 'either on their request or otherwise' was first recommended by the:
new.x: The idea came from the 1st ARC; Punchhi later recommended suo motu deployment in communal violence.

new.s: Under the Punchhi recommendations, the agenda of the Inter-State Council was to be set:
o: By the Union Home Ministry alone
new.x: Punchhi wanted the Inter-State Council to be a working forum whose agenda is set in consultation with the States.

new.s: Before Parliament legislates on a Concurrent List subject, Punchhi wanted broad agreement with the States reached through the:
new.x: The Commission recommended consulting the States through the Inter-State Council before Concurrent List legislation.

new.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that the periods of the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission be synchronised with the:
new.x: It wanted the Finance and Planning Commissions to coordinate, with their time periods synchronised with the Five Year Plans.

new.s: The 16th Finance Commission kept the States' vertical share of the divisible pool at:
new.x: The 16th Finance Commission (2026-31) kept the vertical share at 41%, which the Centre accepted in Budget 2026-27.

new.s: Which of the following Finance Commission – Chairman pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The 14th FC was chaired by Y.V. Reddy, the 15th by N.K. Singh and the 16th by Arvind Panagariya.

new.s: In how many volumes was the Punchhi Commission's report submitted?
new.x: The 2010 report ran to 7 volumes with 273 recommendations.

new.s: Punchhi recommendations were taken up at the Inter-State Council meeting of 16 July 2016, which was its:
new.x: The 11th ISC meeting (16 July 2016), the first in about a decade, took up the Punchhi recommendations.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the status of the Punchhi recommendations:
1. Article 156 has been amended to drop the pleasure clause.
2. Governors still act as Chancellors of State universities.
new.x: Only 2 is correct; Article 156 is unchanged and Governors still hold office during the pleasure of the President.

new.s: Which judgment of 8 April 2025 laid down fixed timelines for Governors on Bills?
o: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor
State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
new.x: State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (8 April 2025) fixed timelines; the Presidential Reference opinion (20 Nov 2025) said courts cannot impose them.

new.s: The Kurian Joseph Committee (2025) on Centre-State relations was set up by the government of:
new.x: The three-member Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed by Tamil Nadu, like the Rajamannar Committee of 1969.

new.s: Which body on Centre-State relations was appointed by a State government in 1969?
new.x: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu; Sarkaria and the First ARC were Centre-appointed.

new.s: The Committee of Governors headed by Bhagwan Sahay, set up in 1970, submitted its report in:
new.x: The Bhagwan Sahay Committee was set up in 1970 and reported in 1971.

new.s: Which of the following did NOT deal with Centre-State relations?
new.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with electoral reform (State funding of elections); the other three dealt with Centre-State relations.

new.s: The First ARC's study team on Centre-State relations was headed by:
new.x: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team; Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiah chaired the ARC itself.

new.s: In 1969 the First Administrative Reforms Commission asked for:
o: Abolition of the office of Governor
new.x: The First ARC was the first to ask for an Inter-State Council under Article 263, with the PM, Central ministers and Chief Ministers.

new.s: How many recommendations on Centre-State relations did the First ARC make?
new.x: The First ARC made 22 recommendations on Centre-State relations, on which no action was taken at the time.

new.s: According to the Bhagwan Sahay Committee, the Governor keeps watch on the State administration and reports to the:
new.x: The Committee saw the Governor as the constitutional head of the State and a link with the Centre, reporting to the Centre.

new.s: An All India Judicial Service and a National Judicial Commission were proposed by the:
new.x: The NCRWC proposed the National Judicial Commission; the Second ARC proposed a National Judicial Council.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Centre-State chapter of the NCRWC:
1. It sought greater fiscal autonomy for States.
2. It sought safeguards against misuse of Article 356.
3. It sought a weaker third tier of local bodies.
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the NCRWC wanted a stronger, not weaker, third tier.

new.s: Which judicial body was proposed by the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
new.x: The Second ARC proposed a National Judicial Council (2007-08); the National Judicial Commission and AIJS were NCRWC proposals.

new.s: 'Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution', dealing with inter-state and regional conflicts, was the Second ARC's:
new.x: The 7th report covered conflict resolution; the 5th was Public Order, the 6th Local Governance and the 15th State and District Administration.

new.s: Centre-State questions such as police and the Inter-State Council usually go before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on:
new.x: Centre-State issues like police, education and the Inter-State Council usually go to the Standing Committee on Home Affairs.

new.s: The Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council, set up in 1996, is chaired by the:
new.x: The Standing Committee of the ISC is chaired by the Union Home Minister; the Inter-State Council itself is chaired by the PM.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Standing Committee on Rural Development's reports on devolution to Panchayats:
1. Panchayats are a State subject.
2. Devolution of functions, finances and functionaries is uniform across States.
new.x: Only 1 is correct; as Panchayats are a State subject, devolution is left to each State and varies across States.

new.s: In May 2018, the Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council finished discussing all 273 recommendations of the:
new.x: It completed discussion of all 273 Punchhi recommendations in May 2018.

new.s: The Inter-State Council (1990), the only recommendation of these bodies to become an institution, came on the advice of the:
new.x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.

new.s: The Kurian Joseph Committee said federalism needs a structural reset comparable in ambition to the economic reforms of:
new.x: It called for a reset comparable to the economic reforms of 1991.

new.s: The term 'cooperative federalism' for India is associated with:
new.x: Granville Austin called Indian federalism cooperative federalism.

new.s: Who described Indian federalism as 'bargaining federalism'?
new.x: Morris-Jones used 'bargaining federalism'; Wheare called India quasi-federal and Austin cooperative.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: K.C. Wheare called India quasi-federal; Ivor Jennings spoke of a federation with a centralising tendency.

new.s: The National Development Council was created in:
new.x: The NDC was created by executive resolution in 1952; the Planning Commission came in 1950.

new.s: Who became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in April 2026?
new.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri became Vice-Chairperson in April 2026, after Suman K. Bery.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It was set up by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015.
2. It has the power to allocate plan grants to States.
new.x: Only 1 is correct; NITI Aayog is advisory and has no power to allocate plan grants.

new.s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog took over the role of the:
new.x: The Governing Council, first constituted in February 2015, took over the NDC's role.

new.s: The 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, where Swarna Andhra @2047 was presented, was held on:
new.x: The 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026; the Council was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in February 2021.

new.s: In the GST Council, the Centre's share of the total votes is:
new.x: The Centre holds one-third and the States together two-thirds of the votes.

new.s: A criticism of the GST Council model of cooperative federalism is that it:
o: Gave the Centre two-thirds of the votes
Was created by a Cabinet resolution
Is chaired by the Union Home Minister
new.x: Subsuming local taxes curtailed States' taxing powers, and compensation disputes followed; the Centre has only one-third of the votes.

new.s: Zonal Councils were set up under the:
new.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, chaired by the Union Home Minister.

new.s: The North Eastern Council was set up in:
new.x: The North Eastern Council dates from 1971.

new.s: For North-Eastern and Himalayan States, the Centre-State funding ratio of core Centrally Sponsored Schemes is:
new.x: Core CSS are funded 60:40, but 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

new.s: In BRAP 2019 (Ease of Doing Business), Andhra Pradesh ranked:
new.x: AP was 1st in BRAP 2019, with Uttar Pradesh 2nd and Telangana 3rd.

new.s: In the Export Preparedness Index 2022, Andhra Pradesh ranked ____ overall.
new.x: AP was 8th overall and 5th among coastal States; Tamil Nadu was 1st.

new.s: NITI Aayog published the School Education Quality Index with the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
new.x: SEQI was published by NITI Aayog with the MHRD; the State Health Index involved MoHFW and the World Bank.

new.s: In the 4th round of the State Health Index (2019-20), Andhra Pradesh's rank among larger States was:
new.x: AP was 4th among larger States, after Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

new.s: Swachh Survekshan rankings are published by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
new.x: Swachh Survekshan is by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not NITI Aayog.

new.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme, launched by NITI Aayog in January 2018, covers how many districts?
new.x: The ADP covers 112 districts.

new.s: Which Andhra Pradesh district from the original list remains in the Aspirational Districts Programme?
new.x: YSR Kadapa stays; Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam replaced Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram.

new.s: Which Andhra Pradesh district ranked 1st in India in the ADP Basic Infrastructure theme (March 2026)?
new.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district ranked 1st in the Basic Infrastructure theme.
